escena: SCENE (equipment bench at night, extreme close-up, NOBODY IN FRAME except one hand): THE SHADOW IS THE SUBJECT. A hard low light from the left throws a LONG, SHARP, GRAPHIC shadow across a brushed dark metal bench, and that shadow is the most detailed thing in the picture: it is the silhouette of a connector held just above the surface. Beside the shadow, on the bench itself, sits the socket it is being offered to — and the shadow and the socket DO NOT MATCH: the silhouette is unmistakably a different shape, wider and with the wrong keying. The two forms lie side by side so the mismatch reads instantly, without a word. A hand enters from the right holding the connector, cut by the frame edge, stopped mid-air: it has not been forced in. A glowing cool blue status light on the equipment throws a soft secondary glow. A small orange sculpture sits further back on the bench, out of focus. 100mm macro lens at f/4, focus on the shadow. The whole frame is COOL and contemporary: daylight-neutral white balance, blue-leaning shadows, nothing warm, amber, golden or tungsten anywhere, no retro glow — the ONLY warm colour in the entire picture is the small orange sculpture itself. Everything except the sculpture is completely unbranded and no text anywhere is readable: any markings on the equipment are tiny, angled and out of focus.

lecho.objeto: the near edge of the metal bench crossing the very bottom against the lens, outside the raking light

texto.muro: the dark unlit back panel of the equipment rising behind the bench, evenly toned, its brushed metal texture visible
